studies.Screening Record ID: 21203820|Calcium|Bladder cancer#gender=mixed sex; 171 men and 27 women among cases and 226 men and 151 women among controls;measurement=dietary_intake
studies.Population: Adults aged 50 years and older from Limburg, including incident histologically confirmed transitional cell carcinoma of the bladder cases and randomly selected controls
studies.Gender: Mixed sex; 171 men and 27 women among cases and 226 men and 151 women among controls
studies.Smoking Status: Mixed; current and non-current smokers included
studies.Ethnicity Basis: NA: no field-specific ethnicity evidence was available
studies.Reference: Dietary intake of micronutrients and the risk of developing bladder cancer: results from the Belgian case-control study on bladder cancer risk.
studies.Authors: Brinkman MT, Buntinx F, Kellen E, Dagnelie PC, Van Dongen MC, Muls E, Zeegers MP
studies.Timing: Dietary intake during the 12 months before interview; incident cases identified between 1999 and 2004
studies.comparison_type: Highest tertile versus lowest tertile of daily calcium intake

sample_size.excerpt: Therefore, dietary data from a total of 198 cases and 377 controls were included in the analyses of this study. Table 1 presents the study characteristics of the participants in the Belgian case–control study on bladder cancer.
sample_size.location: Results, paragraph 1; total_n derived from reported group counts 198 + 377 = 575

cases.excerpt: Therefore, dietary data from a total of 198 cases and 377 controls were included in the analyses of this study.

effect_size.excerpt: A positive association was observed between intake of calcium and bladder cancer (OR: 1.77; 95% CI: 1.00–3.15; p -trend = 0.049).

confidence_interval.excerpt: A positive association was observed between intake of calcium and bladder cancer (OR: 1.77; 95% CI: 1.00–3.15; p -trend = 0.049).

p_value.excerpt: A positive association was observed between intake of calcium and bladder cancer (OR: 1.77; 95% CI: 1.00–3.15; p -trend = 0.049).

comparison.excerpt: We compared the odds for tertile intake categories between cases and controls, with the lowest tertile of intake as the reference category.

timing.excerpt: Participants were asked to report their usual dietary intake for the 12 months prior to the interview.
